rules.rule: JSDoc is required on interfaces, types, functions, and interface fields
Functions must have explicit TypeScript return types
Function parameters must have explicit type annotations
Use @blueprint/time-utils constants (ONE_MINUTE, ONE_HOUR, ONE_DAY, etc.) for time durations in milliseconds instead of magic numbers
TypeBox request body schemas should follow naming convention: <entity><action>Body (e.g., userCreateBody, userUpdateBody)
TypeBox query parameter schemas should follow naming convention: <entity><action>Query (e.g., userListQuery)
TypeBox response schemas should follow naming convention: <entity><action>Response (e.g., userResponse, userListResponse)
Database queries should be centralized in service.ts files as reusable helper functions, not written inline in routes
Use custom error classes from shared/utils/errors.ts (AppError, UnauthorizedError, ForbiddenError, NotFoundError, BadRequestError, ConflictError) instead of throwing generic errors
Module structure: index.ts for Elysia routes, model.ts for TypeBox schemas, service.ts for business logic and database queries
Use Promise.all with map for parallel async operations instead of sequential awaits when operations are independent
Service functions should use a single object parameter with named properties instead of positional arguments (e.g., updateUser({ userId, user, tx }) instead of updateUser(userId, user, tx))
